phasing_details.phase_detail: single phase (to be complete any time within approved condition period)

description: Installation of 1No. BT Street Hub Unit and associated advertisement panels on either side of the unit
decision_conditions: <p><span id="docs-internal-guid-700edb00-7fff-58a3-9356-2888300818e9"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The proposed StreetHub fails to contribute to a safe shared pedestrian and cycle. The introduction of a large digital advertisement introduces unnecessary distraction and a physical obstruction on the public footpath, contrary to highway safety. Furthermore, reducing the width of the footpath in an area that already contains street furniture, reduces the amount of pavement available for the free-flow of pedestrians and cycles without obstruction, harmful to the quality and safety of the walking/cycling environment. As such, the proposal would be contrary to policies D8 (Public realm) and T2 (Healthy streets) of the London Plan (2021) and policies PP1 (Public Realm), PP8 (Hackney Central and Surrounds), LP7 (Advertisements), LP41 (Liveable Neighbourhoods), and LP42 (Walking and Cycling) of Hackney’s Local Development Plan (2020).</span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-c0537331-7fff-8f43-04d8-1790dc00b108"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The proposed StreetHub, by reason of its size, scale, detailed design and appearance, and illumination, featuring a moving digital display, would result in an obtrusive and visually incongruous feature that contributes to an unsightly proliferation and clutter of signage and street furniture in the local area that would detract from the design, character, and appearance of the Clapton Square Conservation Area. As such, the proposal would be contrary to policies D3 (Optimising site capacity through the design-led approach), D4 (Delivering good design), D8 (Public realm), and HC1 (Heritage conservation and growth) of the London Plan (2021) and policies PP1 (Public Realm), PP8 (Hackney Central and Surrounds), LP1 (High Quality Design), LP3 (Designated Heritage Assets), and LP7 (Advertisements) of Hackney's Local Development Plan LP33 (2020), and the </span><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Public Realm Strategy SPD (2012).</span></span></p>
